opensidian 0.9.3 is a bug-fix release on top of 0.9.2. It adds no new file formats or packages: the downloads are the same as 0.9.2 (two AppImages, Flatpak, RPM, DEB) for Linux x86_64.

**This is a draft. SHA256SUMS is not GPG-signed yet.** The maintainer signs it offline before the release is published.

## Fixes

### Editor
- Select text, then type `[[`, `**`, `*` (or another pair character such as `"`, `'`, `(`, `` ` ``): the selection is wrapped instead of replaced. `[[` over a selection no longer opens the link suggester. (#43, PR #53)
- A checked sub-task in a nested checklist is struck through only on its text, not across the whole line including the indent. (#45, PR #56)
- Checklists: moving the cursor up or down onto a checklist row puts it after `- [ ] `, at the start of the task text, and the checkbox stays rendered. This also works for tasks inside quotes, and Up/Down with modifier keys is left alone. (#46, PR #62)
- `==highlight==` text is now drawn in the theme's normal text colour instead of black, and the dark-theme highlight colour matches Obsidian. (#47, PR #54)
- Dropping rich text (for example from a web page) into the editor keeps its formatting and links, converted to Markdown, instead of flattening it to plain text. Plugins that handle drops still run first and can cancel it. (#51, PR #65)

### Files, bookmarks and PDFs
- You can drag a note from the file explorer or from Bookmarks onto a pane to open it in a new tab, or onto a pane edge to open it in a split. (#40, PR #55)
- Clicking a PDF in the file explorer or in Bookmarks opens it in a PDF view. PDF bookmarks have their own menu (open, reveal, remove), removing a PDF bookmark never removes a note with the same name, and PDF bookmarks no longer show a blank label. (#44, PR #57)

### Canvas and Excalidraw
- Excalidraw boards can be bookmarked (they are bookmarked as their note, like in Obsidian). (#48, PR #63)
- A click on the canvas closes the menu that a right-click opened. (#49, PR #52)
- Excalidraw follows opensidian's dark/light mode by default, and its own settings are kept intact. (#50, PR #64)

### Window and Wayland
- Dragging the window by the tab bar on Wayland works every time. Before, every other drag did nothing: the press handed to the compositor was never released inside the app. (#71)
- After maximizing and un-maximizing, the window goes back to its normal size and position. Before, the size from the moment of maximizing could be saved as the normal size.
- Switching vaults from a sandboxed (Landlock) window now closes the old window. Before, it could stay open when `/proc` hides other processes (`hidepid`).

### Plugins and security
- New native dialogs, drawn outside the web view, ask before a vault becomes trusted and before a plugin starts a program or opens a local file with the system opener. The choices are Deny (the default, and what Escape does), Allow once, or Allow for this session. (PR #41, PR #42)
- The program a plugin asks to start is the one that runs. It is resolved once, kept open while you are asked, checked again just before it starts, and a file swapped or replaced by a symlink while the dialog is open is refused. The child gets a clean `PATH` with no entries inside the vault. (PR #41, PR #42)
- Plugin error codes that contain digits (such as `E2BIG`) are reported correctly instead of as a generic I/O error.

### Packaging and build
- Releases are now built on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners by `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Every third-party action is pinned to a commit SHA, and every file has a GitHub build-provenance attestation. Nothing is signed in CI.
- The Flatpak metadata lists the 0.9.2 and 0.9.3 releases.
- Tests and test instrumentation only (no change for users): a test that failed to load, the window-title test hooks (now opt-in), and canvas backlink readings.

## Known issues
- **Reading view scroll sync:** switching to reading view in the middle of a long note sometimes lands 14 to 18 lines away from where you were. It happens only some of the time, and 0.9.2 already had it. Not fixed in this release.

## Verification
Download every file of this release into one directory, then:

```sh
# 1. checksums: every file must report OK
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 2. build provenance: each file was built by this repository's
#    release workflow on GitHub Actions
for f in opensidian-0.9.3-x86_64* SHA256SUMS; do
  gh attestation verify "$f" -R jpzk/opensidian
done
```

**Still to come:** the maintainer's GPG signature of SHA256SUMS (`SHA256SUMS.asc`). It is added before this draft is published. Once it is there, check it with `gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS`.
